about: Corridor line geometry for rail.html. Rail lines follow Natural Earth 1:10m railroads (public domain) between cited stations (shortest path on the rail graph, Douglas-Peucker simplified: hi = 1.5 km, lo = 4 km, 3 decimals). Generalised at 1:10M, so geometric length runs 2-5% shorter than timetable km; on-screen distances always use the cited sources, never the line length. approx = lines opened after the Natural Earth snapshot or missing from it, drawn station to station (the Caucasus link Tbilisi–Marabda–Tsalka–Akhalkalaki–Kartsakhi–Kars follows the Baku–Tbilisi–Kars stations; gauge change 1,520/1,435 mm at Akhalkalaki). sea = maritime links, not rail. Sea links show a connection, not a sailing track (Busan-Vladivostok follows the East Sea coast; Aktau-Alat rounds the Absheron peninsula). routes = the full line chain each corridor actually runs on (its own line, then the shared TSR trunk from the junction, then Moscow-Brest); the screen highlights the whole chain when a corridor is chosen. countries = faint base-layer country names with candidate anchors and a minimum zoom. The Moscow-St Petersburg link (MOW_SPB) is drawn station to station along the October Railway (Moscow-Tver-Vyshny Volochyok-Bologoye-Okulovka-Chudovo-Tosno-Shushary-St Petersburg); its coordinates come from the cited public gazetteers, not from the Natural Earth rail graph. Links past the four corridors (OMS_AST, MOI_SHU, ARY_TAS) let the cargo transport map follow a rail leg beyond them, and the corridor map draws them as spur links like MOW_SPB (corr *, role alt, n = spur name shown in the line tooltip). They are drawn station to station (approx) from OpenStreetMap station nodes, and each end reuses the existing line vertex or station it joins: OMS_AST = Omsk-Cherlak-Valikhanovo-Karasuk-Slavgorod-Kulunda-Sharbakty-Pavlodar-Ekibastuz-Ereymentau-Sorokovaya (Astana); MOI_SHU = Mointy-Sary-Shagan-Shyganak-Khantau-Shu; ARY_TAS = Arys-Darbaza-Saryagash-Keles-Chukursay (Tashkent). Together with TSR, TCR and TCR_MID they follow the station sequence a Vladivostok-Tashkent rail shuttle reported (TSR-Omsk-Karasuk-Pavlodar-Astana-Karaganda-Mointy-Shu-Taraz-Shymkent-Arys-Saryagash-Chukursay). The South Siberian link (TAY_KUL, src G4) follows OpenStreetMap railway ways tagged usage=main (Overpass API query, data as of 2026-11-06, ODbL; a few untagged main-line ways fill the Bardino–Erunakovo–Artyshta II gap) between the cited stations Tayshet–Sayanskaya–Koshurnikovo–Kuragino–Minusinsk–Abakan–Askiz–Biskamzha–Mezhdurechensk–Myski–Polosukhino–Bardino–Erunakovo–Artyshta II–Zarinskaya–Shpagino–Ukladochny–Altayskaya–Barnaul–Kulunda (shortest path, same Douglas-Peucker simplification; mountain loops whose turn exceeds 120 degrees within 8 km are straightened). Its east end reuses the TSR vertex at Tayshet and its west end the OMS_AST vertex at Kulunda; the corridor map draws it as a spur link. fallback = the cargo transport map routes over such a line only when the corridor network cannot reach a leg end or a reported station within 60 km, so an unreported Vladivostok–Chukursay leg keeps the corridor route above, while a leg whose shuttle reported Bardino, Polosukhino or Altayskaya (stations a Vladivostok–Tashkent shuttle reported in November 2026) is drawn through them. Two more links of the same kind (src G4, OpenStreetMap railway ways tagged as running lines, Overpass API query 2026-11-06, ODbL; shortest path between the cited stations, same Douglas-Peucker simplification): NSK_ALT = Novosibirsk-Glavny–Berdsk–Iskitim–Cherepanovo–Altayskaya (the Novosibirsk–Barnaul section of the Turksib; north end on the TSR vertex at Novosibirsk, south end on the TAY_KUL vertex at Altayskaya) and YUR_ART = Yurga I–Topki–Leninsk-Kuznetsky I–Belovo–Artyshta II (the Kuzbass line; north end on the TSR vertex at Yurga, south end on the TAY_KUL vertex at Artyshta II). Both are fallback links drawn as spur links. The Kulunda–Sharbakty–Pavlodar–Ekibastuz–Ereymentau–Sorokovaya section of OMS_AST was checked against the same OpenStreetMap ways (a continuous running line, cited stations within 0.5 km of it), so a shuttle reported west of Barnaul (Rebrikha, Panovo) continues over Kulunda into Kazakhstan on the existing link. Two more fallback links of the same kind (src G4, OpenStreetMap railway ways tagged usage=main, Overpass API query 2026-11-07 on a public mirror whose data is as of 2026-06-01, ODbL; shortest path between the cited stations, same Douglas-Peucker simplification): TAY_TYN = the Baikal–Amur Mainline Tayshet–Vikhorevka–Lena (Ust-Kut)–Severobaikalsk–Novaya Chara–Tynda (west end on the TSR vertex at Tayshet, east of the station where the line leaves the Tayshet yard, the same vertex as TAY_KUL; east end shared with TYN_BAM at Tynda) and TYN_BAM = the Little BAM Tynda–Anosovskaya–Bamovskaya (south end on the TSR vertex between Bamovskaya and Goreliy, where the Amur–Yakutsk tracks reach the TSR). Mountain loops are straightened as on TAY_KUL, except the switchback east of Semigorsk, which is kept because straightening it would move the line more than 5 km from the track. MOW_KOT (src G4, OpenStreetMap ways tagged usage=main, Overpass API query 2026-11-07, ODbL) follows the modern Trans-Siberian course Moscow (Kursky)–Vladimir–Kovrov I–Dzerzhinsk–Nizhny Novgorod-Moskovsky–Semyonov–Shakhunya–Kotelnich I (shortest path between the cited stations, same Douglas-Peucker simplification); its west end is the Moscow (Kursky) station point, 2.3 km from the shared Moscow vertex, which the cargo transport map joins (a line starting on the shared vertex would touch the TSR end there, which the corridor map counts as a crossing); it carries a vertex at Orekhovo-Zuyevo, put on its own segment (0.09 km) where ORZ_KUB starts; its east end is the TSR vertex at Kotelnich I, and the vertex before it, north of the TSR, is dropped so the line does not cross the TSR (1.7 km). Drawn as a fallback spur link. SHA_EKB (src G4, OpenStreetMap ways tagged usage=main, Overpass API query 2026-11-07, ODbL) follows the Kazan course of the Trans-Siberian Shatura–Cherusti–Murom I–Arzamas-2–Kanash–Zelenodolsk–Kazan-Passazhirskaya–Agryz–Krasnoufimsk–Druzhinino–Yekaterinburg-Sortirovochny (shortest path between the cited stations, same Douglas-Peucker simplification); its west end reuses the TCR vertex at Shatura (TCR already follows the Moscow–Kurovskaya–Shatura main line) and its east end the TSR vertex west of Yekaterinburg-Sortirovochny. Drawn as a fallback spur link. EKB_NTG (src G4, OpenStreetMap ways tagged usage=main, Overpass API query 2026-11-07, ODbL) follows Yekaterinburg-Sortirovochny–Shuvakish–Nevyansk–Nizhny Tagil (shortest path, same Douglas-Peucker simplification); its south end reuses the TSR vertex west of Yekaterinburg-Sortirovochny (shared with SHA_EKB), its north end is free at Nizhny Tagil. Drawn as a fallback spur link. DAN_SPB (src G4, OpenStreetMap running-line ways, Overpass API query 2026-11-07, ODbL; shortest path between the cited stations, same Douglas-Peucker simplification) = Danilov–Vologda I–Cherepovets I–Babaevo–Volkhovstroy I–Mga–Rybatskoye–Kupchinskaya (Shushary freight approach); south end on the TSR vertex near Danilov, north end at Kupchinskaya, on a point put on the MOW_SPB segment (0.3 km), where the line meets the Moscow–St Petersburg link (the former approx run of 13.8 km from Kupchinskaya into the city point, alongside the MOW_SPB approx segment, is dropped). Fallback link drawn as a spur link. ORZ_KUB (src G4, same method) = Greater Moscow Ring Railway Orekhovo-Zuyevo–Kurovskaya–Berendino–Voskresensk–Mikhnevo–Sandarovo–Bekasovo–Kubinka, ending where it meets the Belarus line at Kubinka, on a point put on the MOW_BRE segment 1.8 km from the OSM junction vertex (the former 14 km run west beside MOW_BRE to its vertex near Tuchkovo is dropped; the lo end sits on the MOW_BRE lo segment the same way); the Orekhovo-Zuyevo end sits on the MOW_KOT vertex at Orekhovo-Zuyevo (not a free end), and it crosses TCR at Kurovskaya, a junction listed under crossings. Fallback link drawn as a spur link. EKB_KUR and PET_OMS (src G4, OpenStreetMap railway ways tagged usage=main plus untagged running lines, Overpass API query 2026-11-07, ODbL; shortest path between the cited stations, same Douglas-Peucker simplification) are the two ends of the Yekaterinburg–Kamensk-Uralsky–Shadrinsk–Kurgan–Petropavlovsk–Bulaevo–Isilkul–Omsk line: EKB_KUR = Yekaterinburg–Kamensk-Uralsky–Shadrinsk–Kurgan (west end on the TSR vertex east of Yekaterinburg, east end on the TCR vertex at Kurgan) and PET_OMS = Petropavlovsk–Bulaevo–Isilkul–Omsk (west end on the TCR vertex at Petropavlovsk, east end on the TSR/OMS_AST vertex at Omsk; its last 3.8 km from Omsk-Passazhirsky to that vertex is approx). Between Kurgan and Petropavlovsk the line runs on the same track as TCR (within 2.2 km), so that section is drawn once, as TCR. Two in-station reversals at Kamensk-Uralsky and Kurgan, left by crossovers outside the running-line filter, are closed by a chord under 0.4 km. Fallback links drawn as spur links. Three more fallback links of the same kind (src G4, OpenStreetMap railway ways tagged usage=main plus untagged running lines, one Overpass API query 2026-11-07 on a public mirror, data as of 2026-11-07T04:16:58Z, ODbL; shortest path between the cited stations, gaps under 0.3 km between way ends bridged, in-station reversals closed by a chord under 0.5 km, same Douglas-Peucker simplification): SRS_KAR = the Middle Siberian Railway Srednesibirskaya–Kamen-na-Obi–Khabary–Krasnozyorskoye–Karasuk I (east end on the NSK_ALT line at the Srednesibirskaya junction, west end on the OMS_AST vertex at Karasuk; the shortest main-line path ran on to the junction north-west of Karasuk and turned back 151 degrees into the station, so that vertex is dropped and the line enters Karasuk I from the east, as the usage=branch connecting tracks do); STB_SIL = Stolbovaya–Grivno–Podolsk–Silikatnaya on the Kursk line (south end on the ORZ_KUB line near Stolbovaya, where the connecting line from the Greater Moscow Ring meets the Kursk line; north end free at Silikatnaya); BEK_SEL = Bekasovo I–Selyatino on the Kiev line (west end on the ORZ_KUB line at Bekasovo, east end free at Selyatino; drawn straight along the Kiev line ways, within 0.3 km of them — the earlier path started on a ring track at the Bekasovo I station node and ran 2.9 km south-west through the station and back). free = a dead end at a terminal: the screens do not join it to another line that passes within 25 km (EKB_NTG ends the same way at Nizhny Tagil). overview = cargo: on the first, whole-network view of the corridor map such a line is drawn only when a shown container lies within 60 km of it (TAY_TYN, TYN_BAM run far north of the TSR; zooming in always shows them). endsOnly = a line the cargo transport map routes over only when a leg end or a reported station lies within 60 km of a line of that group: BAM (TAY_TYN, TYN_BAM), GORKY (MOW_KOT), KAZAN (SHA_EKB), KURGAN (EKB_KUR, PET_OMS), VOLOGDA (DAN_SPB) and SRS (SRS_KAR) run beside the TSR or an earlier link and are shorter on the line graph, so a leg without a report on them keeps the route it had before (a Far East–South Siberia leg keeps the TSR). UKL_SRS (src G4, the same OpenStreetMap ways and method as SRS_KAR, Overpass query 2026-11-07, data as of 2026-11-07T04:16:58Z, ODbL) is the connecting line from the South Siberian line west of Ukladochny north past Novopovalikha to the Novosibirsk–Barnaul line north of Povalikha (shortest path towards Srednesibirskaya, end trimmed where it runs on NSK_ALT): its south end is a point put on the TAY_KUL segment and its north end a point put on the NSK_ALT segment, so a leg from the South Siberian line to the Middle Siberian Railway (a shuttle reported Shpagino, Ukladochny and then Karasuk I) is drawn without turning back at Altayskaya. Fallback link drawn as a spur link. crossings = junction stations where two drawn lines cross and the OpenStreetMap running lines connect them (Overpass API query 2026-11-07, data as of 2026-11-07T07:46:19Z, ODbL): Kurovskaya, where the Greater Moscow Ring (ORZ_KUB) crosses the Moscow–Kurovskaya–Shatura line (TCR) and tracks lead from the Shatura side to the ring southwards and from the Moscow side to the ring northwards; ll is the point where the two drawn lines cross (2.2 km west of the station node, within the line simplification). The cargo transport map lets a route change lines there; the corridor map draws nothing extra. Line ends: both screens join a line end only to the nearest other line (within 25 km); the cargo transport map draws no straight link longer than 2 km between two lines and instead moves such an end onto the nearest line, as the corridor map draws it.
